subject: Private link: flow-labeling return-path mismatch + MTU/SG observations
messages:
From: NetOps Clearline <netops@clearline.net>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private link cutover — packet truncation and return-path failures

Hi Olga,

We started the last-mile cutover to the private link this morning (10:00 local). Several services are seeing intermittent failures. Symptoms:
- TCP sessions from app hosts to Redwood backends succeed for the SYN/ACK exchange, but mid-stream packets are being dropped (application-level retries).
- Traceroutes from our edge show asymmetry: return traffic traverses an intermediate NAT cluster rather than the direct tunnel.
- We captured a short pcap showing many MSS-exceeded retransmits and some duplicate ACKs.

We haven't changed any SG (security group) rules on our side for this cutover. Attached: clearline_capture_20251001.pcap (excerpt) and our traceroute output.

Can you confirm whether Redwood applied any flow-labeling/connmark changes or sticky SNAT adjustments during the window? This looks like conntrack sticky mappings + MTU forcing causing path differences.

Thanks,
Alex Garcia
NetOps — Clearline Networks

On Wed, Oct 1, 2025 at 09:12 AM NetOps Clearline <netops@clearline.net> wrote:
> We captured a short pcap showing many MSS-exceeded retransmits and some duplicate ACKs.
> We haven't changed any SG rules on our side for this cutover.
> Can you confirm whether Redwood applied any flow-labeling/connmark changes or sticky SNAT adjustments during the window?

Thanks Alex — quick summary of what I'm seeing from our side after an initial sweep:
- Control plane: no deliberate flow-labeling rollout or connmark policy push in the last 48h.
- Data plane: we had a small autoscaling event on the dedicated NAT pool ~09:45 which may have redistributed SNAT affinities across a new cluster node. That can cause apparent return-path mismatches if your route hash prefers the old node.
- MTU: I see fragments in the pcap consistent with PMTU mismatch (we typically clamp MSS at the tunnel endpoint but the peer tunnel negotiation looks to be passing larger packets).

Immediate triage steps performed:
1) Pulled conntrack summaries for the affected vpc and attached an excerpt (redwood_conntrack_excerpt_20251001.log).
2) Checked ECMP hash distribution for the cutover corridor — small imbalance noted.

Suggested quick mitigations (we can do immediately with your sign-off):
- Temporarily pin SNAT affinity for the affected source prefix to the original NAT node (bounded 30m).
- Add an MTU clamp at the ingress tunnel endpoint at 1400 to test whether fragmentation disappears.
- As a parallel check, expand the SG ingress rule for the specific ephemeral port range (we'll restrict to the prefix in your traceroute).

If you prefer, we can apply the SNAT pin and MTU clamp as a canary and monitor for 30 minutes.

-Markus
Network Lead, Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks, that matches our suspicion re: SNAT churn.

We ran an additional traceroute from the app egress cluster (attached). The traceroute shows return hops going through their NAT cluster (10.240.x.x) instead of the MPLS backhaul peer. We did not apply any SG changes on our side during the window; our change window only included BGP next-hop adjustments which should not affect port affinity.

We approve:
- SNAT affinity pin for src prefix 198.51.100.0/24 for 30 minutes
- MTU clamp test to 1400 at the Redwood tunnel ingress

We'll monitor and report back in 15 minutes.

Alex Garcia

Subject: Re: Private link cutover — packet truncation and return-path failures

Update and close: thank you all for rapid coordination. Summary of actions and outcome: 
- 2025-10-01 11:15 UTC: applied SNAT affinity pin for 198.51.100.0/24 to original NAT node (30m).
- 2025-10-01 11:18 UTC: enabled MTU clamp at 1400 on the Redwood tunnel ingress.
- 2025-10-01 11:21 UTC: Clearline reported reduced retransmits and no MSS fragmentation in a 20m observation window.
- 2025-10-02 08:10 UTC: expanded temporary SG allowlist for 198.51.100.0/24 to debug ports 9000-9020 (timebox 12h).

Root cause (post-mortem): an autoscaling event moved ephemeral SNAT state during the cutover, exposing an ECMP/route-hash mismatch that caused return traffic to route through a different NAT cluster. The combination of larger-than-expected PMTU and the sticky SNAT redistribution amplified application-visible retries.

Next steps / follow-ups (short list):
- We will add a small pre-cutover check to avoid SNAT node churn during customer-invoked cutovers (Playbook:PRIVATE-CUTOVER-NAT-MTU).
- Engineering will pilot persistent SNAT affinity for known cutover prefixes and surface an alert if ECMP imbalance exceeds threshold (JIRA:TROUBLE-4123).
- I'll share the conntrack excerpt and pcap to the private drive folder (link above) for the postmortem.

Please reply if you need an extended retention of logs or a formal RC. Otherwise I'll mark this as resolved in the ticket.

Olga Petrov
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
